1 · The Mission Challenge

Why Landing Near the Lunar South Pole Is Hard

75°S – 90°S · ±150 km Mosaic

1. Grazing 1.54° Sunlight Creates Extremes

  • Crater rims glow up to 90% of the year while adjacent floors stay in 40 K eternal shadow (PSR).

2. High Sunlight Does Not Mean Good Comms

  • Earth libration shifts independently: Connecting Ridge gets 90% Sun but 55% DTE; Mons Mouton gets 100% DTE vs 45% Sun.

3. Planetary Data Was Disconnected

  • LOLA elevation files, JPL orbits, and Artemis III polygons lived in separate tools—hard for teams and students to test live.
Our Solution: Interactive 360° Ray-Marching Browser Engine

Composite Viability Formula (0–100 Heuristic)

Σw = 1.00 · Convex MCDA
0.35 SunDisk + 0.25 DTE + 0.15 Joint + 0.15 Dark(30d) + 0.10 Slope≤5°
50% Power & Night Survival
40% Comms + Overlap
10%
  • 50% Energy & Night (Mazarico/Gläser): Mean solar disk fraction (no grazing slivers) + 30-day synodic blackout cap.
  • 40% Direct Comms + Sun∩Earth: Captures independent Earth libration & sunlit teleoperation overlap.
  • 10% HLS Slope (≤5° on 240 m): Bounded to prevent coarse-grid overconfidence; returns n/a outside DEM.

Honest Boundary #1: 240 m Screening

  • Models macro horizon shadows & DTE—not meter-scale boulders. Next stage uses 5 m PGDA & 1 m LROC NAC.

Honest Boundary #2: Clear n/a Scope

  • Viability is a transparent heuristic (not HLS certification). Targets north of 75°S report n/a for DEM slope.

Automated CI Guardrails

  • 10 Python + 68 Vitest (+ 34 todo) tests lock binary DEM byte parity, custom pin parity (≤ 2 pp), and both ≤ min(sun, earth).
